entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
225 of 2023 at Police Station Nandgram, District Ghaziabad under Sections 498A, 323, 304B I.P.C.
and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.
The applicant is in jail since 15.04.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 18.07.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Akash Mishra, learned counsel holding brief of Shri Santosh Singh, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Mohd.
Afzal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Shivam vs State Of U.P. on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63269284/
1
1. The applicant is the second husband of the deceased.
The first marriage of the deceased ended unhappily.
2. The applicant never tortured the deceased or demanded dowry.
3. The relations between the couple were harmonious.
4. The deceased was a sensitive person who often became depressed on account of the trauma of her failed first marriage.
5. On the fateful day, she succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by consuming a poisonous substance.
6. When the poison began to take effect, the applicant promptly rushed the deceased to hospital but to no avail.
The deceased was declared dead on arrival at the hospital.
7. The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
8. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and shows no signs of an early conclusion.
The applicant cannot be faulted for the delay in the trial.
9. The first informant who is the mother of the deceased has repudiated the prosecution case in her testimony before the trial court.
The victim has been declared hostile at the instance of the prosecution.
10. Prosecution witnesses are deliberately delaying the trial only to prolong the incarceration of the applicant.
11. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite detention of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.

Right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.
12.
The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Shivam be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The Shivam vs State Of U.P. on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63269284/
2 following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties, or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
